release: Autonomous pass over the highest-value unfinished work. Four units, none of which crossed the Architecture Freeze. GZIPPED SITEMAPS ARE PARSED. They were recorded present-and-unread because getText decodes UTF-8, which destroys gzip bytes; zlib is a builtin so this cost no dependency. Gzip is detected by MAGIC BYTES, covering a raw .gz file, a Content-Encoding gzip response, and a .gz extension on plain XML. Decompression is capped at 64 MB because a few hundred bytes of gzip can encode gigabytes and an unbounded gunzip in a tool that fetches attacker-controlled URLs is a denial-of-service the AUDITED SITE can aim at the operator. Size accounting uses the UNCOMPRESSED length, or a 2 MB gzip carrying 80 MB of XML would pass a limit it plainly breaks. THE TWO NUMBERS EXPLAIN THEMSELVES. A run read 'score 50, quality 84, PASSED WITH WARNINGS' with no statement of what any of them measures and two apparently contradicting. Both are now labelled and carry the reason they differ: one is the share of GRADED checks that passed, weighting every check equally; the other is registry-weighted over rules that provably ran, so one critical failure costs more than ten minor ones. Presentation only - the scoring model is frozen and nothing recomputes it. TEST-SUITE ENVIRONMENT SWEEP, after the PID-modulo port. ui-script.test.js derived its port from hrtime and then CONNECTED to it, the same silent talk-to-a-stranger class; it now asks the OS for a free port AND aborts if the spawned child died, so asserting against another process is impossible rather than unlikely. Two fixture suites moved off fixed ports. AND THE REAL FIND: three suites pin assertions to stored live runs that HAVE BEEN DELETED, so roughly fourteen assertions in readiness plus the anti-fixture cross-check in score-evaluation have been silently dead while the run reported 66/66. Not fixable by inventing baselines - re-pinning to a current run means deriving expectations from today's behaviour, the exact trap those suites exist to prevent. The skip is now LOUD and NAMES the missing artifacts. CERTIFICATION.md MATCHES THE PRODUCT AGAIN. The record that answers 'can this ship' claimed engine 2.4.0, registry 1.13.0, 142 rules, package 4.5.0 and 58 suites while the product was 4.1.0, 1.15.0, 161, 6.2.0 and 66 - drifted through two majors with nothing to catch it. Reconciled, and now GUARDED by verifyCertification() in the version-authority suite, with a negative control that proves the verifier reports dirty on a deliberately stale copy.
